items.title: Boundary gate precedes promotion
items.statement: The diagnostics gate runs at enabled phase, task, or subtask boundaries before promotion; the default boundary is phase, and an iteration-local preflight is advisory only.

evidence.exact_quote: - **When it runs:** At configured **tier boundaries** before promotion. It MAY be enabled for `phase`, `task`, and/or `subtask`; default: **phase boundary only**. Implementations MAY also run an iteration-local preflight, but that is advisory and MUST NOT replace the configured boundary gate.

items.title: Gate scope modes and default
items.statement: The gate exposes changed_files, open, and project scopes and defaults to changed_files.

evidence.exact_quote: - **`project`** -- All project files that have an LSP server (bounded: e.g. under project root, or only files with open documents). Default: **`changed_files`** to keep checks fast and relevant.

items.title: Diagnostic blocking threshold
items.statement: The source defines an errors-only threshold and an errors-plus-warnings threshold, with errors-only as the default and Info ignored by either blocking mode.

evidence.exact_quote: - **`error`** -- Gate passes if there are **no diagnostics with severity Error** in scope. Warnings and Info are ignored.
- **`error_and_warning`** -- Gate passes if there are **no diagnostics with severity Error or Warning** in scope. Info is ignored.

items.title: Verification UI controls are specified
items.statement: The Verification tab must expose enable, scope, blocking threshold, boundary, and timeout controls bound to the persisted LSP gate config.

evidence.exact_quote: - **GUI:** Verification tab: "LSP diagnostics gate" subsection: Enable checkbox; Scope dropdown (Changed files / Open files / Whole project); Block on (Errors only / Errors and warnings); Tier boundaries (checkboxes: Phase, Task, Subtask); Timeout (seconds). Persist in same config blob as `VerificationConfig` (e.g. extend `VerificationConfig` or nested `lsp_gate`).

items.title: Failed gate follows generic retry or terminal policy
items.statement: A failing LSP criterion marks the tier gate failed and then follows the existing retry, escalation, or stop policy without an LSP-specific branch.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Orchestrator behavior:** Same as for any failed gate: **retry** (next iteration) if retry policy allows; else **escalate** or **stop** per tier config (e.g. `task_failure_style`). No special case for LSP gate.

items.title: Every evaluated gate run captures evidence
items.statement: Whenever the LSP gate runs, it must capture and attach a diagnostics snapshot whether the criterion passes or fails.

evidence.exact_quote: - **When:** When the LSP gate **runs** (whether it passes or fails), attach an **LSP diagnostics snapshot** to the gate report. So: **always** capture snapshot at gate run time; store it as evidence linked to that gate run.

items.title: Verifier registry owns dispatch
items.statement: LspGateVerifier is registered in VerifierRegistry and is selected through the existing criterion verification_method dispatch path.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Who calls LSP:** A new verifier **`LspGateVerifier`** (or **`lsp_gate_verifier`**), registered in `VerifierRegistry` (e.g. in `verifier.rs` `register_defaults`). Criterion type: `verification_method: "lsp"` or `"lsp_gate"`.

items.title: Diagnostics client input and output contract
items.statement: The conceptual client API accepts paths plus project root and returns diagnostic entries containing location, severity, message, and source data.

evidence.exact_quote: - Signature (conceptual): `get_diagnostics_for_paths(paths: &[PathBuf], project_root: &Path) -> Result<Vec<LspDiagnosticEntry>, LspGateError>`.

- Returns: list of diagnostics (path, line, character, severity, message, source) for the given paths. If a path has no server or no diagnostics, it contributes an empty list. The client uses the existing DiagnosticsCache (from `publishDiagnostics`) and/or triggers a request if needed; must respect timeout (e.g. 15 s) and return partial results or error on timeout.

items.title: Evidence coordinate conventions
items.statement: Evidence uses 1-based displayed line numbers and 0-based character offsets, converting line numbers to protocol coordinates only at the LSP boundary.

evidence.exact_quote: - **line** -- 0-based or 1-based per LSP spec (LSP uses 0-based); **Decision:** Store and display 1-based in evidence and UI; convert to 0-based only at the LSP protocol boundary.
- **character** -- Offset in line (0-based).

items.title: Snapshot lifecycle is one artifact per gate run
items.statement: The MVP captures one after-iteration snapshot at evaluation time, writes it under the LSP snapshot evidence directory, attaches its path, and returns pass or fail.

evidence.exact_quote: - **After run (when gate runs):** Yes. When the LSP gate verifier runs (at tier boundary), it captures the snapshot **at that moment** (after iteration, before promotion). So: **one snapshot per gate run** at the time the gate is evaluated.

items.title: LSP subagent bias is optional and non-authoritative
items.statement: Subagent bias defaults off and, when enabled, only ranks or breaks ties; explicit plan requirements, node override lists, and required-subagent contracts take precedence.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Where in the flow:** When the orchestrator is about to **select a subagent for the next node** (task or subtask), it can optionally query LSP diagnostics for **files in scope** for that node. **Decision:** Default **off**. Config key `orchestrator.lsp_subagent_bias` (bool, default false). When true, call `get_diagnostics_for_paths` and apply bias toward matching-language subagent. If any file has diagnostics (e.g. errors) from a language server X, **prefer** the subagent that matches language X (e.g. rust-analyzer → rust-engineer, pyright → python-pro).
- Explicit plan requirements, node override lists, or hard-coded contract needs (for example `required_subagents`) take precedence over LSP bias.

items.title: Unavailable client does not block by default
items.statement: The default unavailable-client behavior is an explicit skip with a diagnostic actual string, so startup unavailability is not implicitly treated as success or failure.

evidence.exact_quote: | **LSP client not ready** | Gate does not run, or runs with a **skip** result. **Decision:** When LSP gate is enabled but client not ready: **skip** the criterion; set `actual: "LSP client not ready"`. Config: `lsp_gate.when_unavailable`: `skip` | `pass` | `fail`, default **skip**. Gate does not block on LSP startup. |

items.title: Timeout failure is explicit
items.statement: A diagnostics query timeout fails the criterion and retains a partial snapshot when partial diagnostics exist.

evidence.exact_quote: | **Timeout when querying diagnostics** | LspGateVerifier uses a timeout (e.g. `timeout_seconds` from config). On timeout: **fail** the criterion with `actual: "LSP diagnostics query timed out"`. Attach partial snapshot if any diagnostics were collected before timeout. |

items.title: No-server and empty-scope outcomes are explicit
items.statement: Files without a language server contribute no diagnostics, and a scope resolving to zero files passes.

evidence.exact_quote: | **No server for language** | For some files in scope there is no LSP server (e.g. unknown extension). Those files contribute **no diagnostics** (empty list). Gate passes for that file; only files with a server are checked. No special failure. |
| **Empty scope (changed_files/open/project)** | If scope resolves to zero files (e.g. no files changed), gate **passes** (nothing to check). |

items.title: Owner and cross-document boundary are explicit
items.statement: LSPSupport remains owner for its preserved LSP behavior while ContractRefs and boundary notes allocate cross-document ownership.

evidence.exact_quote: This source-preserving standardization keeps the owner and consumer boundaries stated in the original document body. During this batch, `Plans/LSPSupport.md` remains the owner doc for the behavior described by its preserved sections, while cross-doc ownership follows the ContractRefs and boundary notes already present in the original text.

items.title: PlanUnit migration validators are named
items.statement: The PlanUnits identify exact migration and index validation commands and require lossless source-span availability and traceability.

evidence.exact_quote: - python3 scripts/pm-plan-migration.py validate --run-dir Plans/.plan_migration/pds-20260611-002-atomize-planunits
- python3 scripts/pm-plan-index.py validate

items.title: Planning output is barred from executable work creation
items.statement: The PlanUnit acceptance contract explicitly forbids creating WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, or production build tasks.

evidence.exact_quote: - No WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, or production build tasks are created.

items.title: Authored copy boundary excludes server payloads
items.statement: Authored LSP tooltip, help, settings, and explanatory copy follows the dual ELI5/Expert contract, while server-returned hover and diagnostics are dynamic external content outside that authored-copy rule.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Authored tooltip, help, settings, and explanatory LSP copy follows the FinalGUISpec dual ELI5/Expert copy contract, while dynamic server-returned hover and diagnostic payloads are outside authored dual-copy enforcement.
- Server-returned hover or diagnostic payloads are dynamic external content and are not authored dual-copy strings.

items.title: Core LSP capability inventory is enumerated
items.statement: The accepted capability inventory covers diagnostics, hover, completion, navigation, inlay hints, semantic highlighting, actions, lenses, signatures, cancellation, status, server disabling, fallback, and Assistant-context diagnostics.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The LSP MVP capability inventory includes diagnostics, hover, autocomplete, navigation, inlay hints, semantic highlighting, code actions, code lens, signature help, timeout/cancellation, LSP status UI, per-server disable, fallback behavior, and diagnostics for LLM/Assistant context.

items.title: Fallback contract forbids fabricated semantic truth
items.statement: The accepted feature matrix preserves inputs, outputs, success, failure, config, and fallback behavior, and explicitly prohibits fabricating diagnostics or semantic-health state when LSP is unavailable.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Each LSP feature preserves its input, output, success, failure, edge-case, config-key, and fallback behavior, including timeout handling, stale-response discard, no-server behavior, and the shared fallback contract when LSP is unavailable.
- Unavailable LSP must not fabricate diagnostics, hover, completion, or healthy semantic capability state.

items.title: Blocking enum tokens conflict
items.statement: The prose threshold tokens are singular (`error`, `error_and_warning`), while the resolved config table requires plural tokens (`errors`, `errors_and_warnings`); no normalization or compatibility rule selects the canonical serialized form.

evidence.exact_quote: - **`error`** -- Gate passes if there are **no diagnostics with severity Error** in scope. Warnings and Info are ignored.
| `block_on` | string | `"errors"` \| `"errors_and_warnings"` | **`"errors"`** |

items.impact: Independent config, UI, and verifier implementations can serialize or match different values, causing settings to be rejected or silently ignored.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must choose a canonical enum and decide whether to accept aliases or migrate older values.

items.title: Unavailable-policy enum conflicts
items.statement: The config schema table permits only skip or fail, but the failure-mode contract adds pass and later says a crash may skip or pass per config.

evidence.exact_quote: | `when_unavailable` | string | `"skip"` \| `"fail"` | **`"skip"`** |

| **LSP client not ready** | Gate does not run, or runs with a **skip** result. **Decision:** When LSP gate is enabled but client not ready: **skip** the criterion; set `actual: "LSP client not ready"`. Config: `lsp_gate.when_unavailable`: `skip` | `pass` | `fail`, default **skip**. Gate does not block on LSP startup. |

items.impact: A `pass` value may be rejected by persistence/UI or interpreted inconsistently by the verifier.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must decide whether pass is supported, remove it from failure behavior, or extend the config contract and migration path.

items.title: Configuration authority and precedence are unresolved
items.statement: The gate is said to live in redb, to be persisted in the VerificationConfig blob, and to be overridden by a project JSON file, but no read/write authority or precedence rule is defined.

evidence.exact_quote: Config key: `verification.lsp_gate` in redb. All values are overridable per project via `.puppet-master/config.json`.

- **VerificationConfig:** Extend the existing verification config (e.g. `VerificationConfig` in `config/gui_config.rs` or equivalent) with an optional **`lsp_gate`** field (nested struct matching the schema above: `enabled`, `scope`, `block_on`, `tier_boundaries`, `timeout_seconds`, optional `when_unavailable`). Persist in the same blob as other verification settings. **Verification tab UI:** Add "LSP diagnostics gate" subsection with controls bound to this struct.

items.impact: The effective configuration can differ depending on whether a caller reads redb, GUI config, or project JSON first.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must define merge order, source of persisted truth, write-back behavior, and conflict handling.

items.title: Global and per-tier override resolution is not specified
items.statement: The source allows a global setting or per-tier overrides and recommends both, but does not define field-level inheritance, replacement, or precedence.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Where:** Verification tab (Settings or Config → Verification). Can be **global** (one setting for all tiers) or **per-tier** (override per phase/task/subtask). Recommendation: global `lsp_gate` with optional per-tier override in tier config.

items.impact: Partially specified tier overrides can produce different effective thresholds, scopes, or timeout behavior.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must choose whole-object replacement or field-level merge semantics and define unset/null behavior.

items.title: Project scope is not a determinate file set
items.statement: Project scope is described both as all project files with an LSP server and as potentially only open documents, leaving the bounded traversal and inclusion rule unresolved.

evidence.exact_quote: - **`project`** -- All project files that have an LSP server (bounded: e.g. under project root, or only files with open documents). Default: **`changed_files`** to keep checks fast and relevant.

items.impact: Two conforming implementations could check radically different files while reporting the same project scope.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must define traversal roots, ignores, symlinks, generated/vendor files, server-capability discovery, and any hard file/count bounds.

items.title: Changed-files interval is ambiguous
items.statement: Changed files may mean the last iteration, current subtask, or files modified in the current tier; the snapshot baseline and behavior at task or phase boundaries are not fixed.

evidence.exact_quote: - **`changed_files`** -- Only files that were modified in the last iteration (or in the current subtask). Requires tracking changed paths (e.g. from git diff or execution engine "files touched").
- `scope`: **"changed_files"** (only check files modified in this tier)

items.impact: The same boundary can pass or fail depending on which change interval is selected.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must choose and persist a baseline per boundary and reconcile git-diff and execution-engine touched-file sources.

items.title: Diagnostic freshness and version binding are absent
items.statement: The client may use the cache or trigger a request, but the source does not define how evaluation proves diagnostics correspond to the post-iteration document version or when stale cached publications are discarded.

evidence.exact_quote: - Returns: list of diagnostics (path, line, character, severity, message, source) for the given paths. If a path has no server or no diagnostics, it contributes an empty list. The client uses the existing DiagnosticsCache (from `publishDiagnostics`) and/or triggers a request if needed; must respect timeout (e.g. 15 s) and return partial results or error on timeout.

items.impact: A gate may pass on an empty stale cache or fail on diagnostics from an older document version.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must define version matching, cache age, request/flush synchronization, stale-response rejection, and partial-result completeness.

items.title: Prompt evidence ranking and summarization are undefined
items.statement: Only the top five evidence items may auto-ingest, but current relevance/severity ranking, stable tie-breaking, and summarization-only behavior are not defined.

evidence.exact_quote: Prompt-consumable LSP/debug evidence may auto-ingest at most the top five evidence items by current relevance `/severity`; after that cap, additional diagnostics or trace material enter summarization-only mode unless the user explicitly opens the full runtime artifact.

items.impact: Different evidence can reach the model for the same snapshot, and summaries may omit gating-relevant details.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must define the score, tie-break order, summarizer inputs/outputs, provenance, and whether all blocking diagnostics bypass the cap.

items.title: Snapshot privacy, retention, and access controls are unspecified
items.statement: Snapshots may contain absolute paths, project roots, and server diagnostic messages, yet the contract defines no redaction, permissions, retention, or deletion policy.

evidence.exact_quote: - **path** -- Relative to project root or absolute; same as LSP URI normalized to path.
- **Content:** Single JSON object: `{ "captured_at": "ISO8601", "scope": "changed_files"|"open"|"project", "project_root": "...", "diagnostics": [ {...}, ... ] }`.

items.impact: Evidence artifacts can expose local filesystem identity, workspace names, source-derived messages, or sensitive paths beyond the active run.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must choose path canonicalization/redaction, artifact permissions, retention, cleanup, and export rules.

items.title: Character offset unit is unspecified
items.statement: The snapshot fixes character offsets as zero-based but does not define the encoding unit or conversion contract, so non-ASCII positions can be rendered inconsistently.

evidence.exact_quote: - **character** -- Offset in line (0-based).

items.impact: Diagnostic highlights and navigation can point to the wrong character for multi-byte or surrogate-pair text.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must define the stored offset encoding and conversions at both protocol and UI boundaries.

items.title: Snapshot envelope lacks completeness and identity fields
items.statement: The declared JSON object contains capture time, scope, project root, and diagnostics but no schema version, gate/run identity, requested path set, unavailable-server list, timeout flag, or completeness marker.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Content:** Single JSON object: `{ "captured_at": "ISO8601", "scope": "changed_files"|"open"|"project", "project_root": "...", "diagnostics": [ {...}, ... ] }`.

items.impact: Consumers cannot distinguish a complete clean snapshot from an empty or partial collection, nor independently bind the artifact to a specific gate evaluation.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must extend or externally wrap the snapshot with identity, coverage, and completeness metadata.

items.title: Snapshot persistence failure has no recovery contract
items.statement: The verifier is required to write and attach a snapshot before returning, but behavior for directory creation, serialization failure, collision, permission denial, or disk exhaustion is not stated.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Gate runner** (via LspGateVerifier). The verifier is invoked by the gate runner when a criterion with `verification_method: "lsp"` is evaluated. The verifier (1) gets diagnostics from LSP client for scope, (2) writes snapshot JSON to `.puppet-master/evidence/lsp-snapshots/`, (3) attaches evidence to VerifierResult (path to snapshot file), (4) returns passed/failed. EvidenceStore (if wired) can also persist the path; GateReport criteria already carry per-criterion evidence from VerifierResult.

items.impact: A gate may return a pass/fail result without its mandatory evidence or may fail nondeterministically for storage reasons.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must decide whether evidence-write failure fails, skips, retries, or rolls back the criterion and how partial files are cleaned up.

items.title: Skip state is not integrated with the result model
items.statement: The failure table alternates between the gate not running and running with a skip result, but the described verifier result and gate criterion fields only establish passed/failed and met/not-met behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Gate fails (LSP errors in scope):** The gate report for that tier has `passed: false`; the **criterion** for the LSP gate has `met: false` and `actual` set to a summary (e.g. "3 LSP errors in scope (see evidence)").

| **LSP client not ready** | Gate does not run, or runs with a **skip** result. **Decision:** When LSP gate is enabled but client not ready: **skip** the criterion; set `actual: "LSP client not ready"`. Config: `lsp_gate.when_unavailable`: `skip` | `pass` | `fail`, default **skip**. Gate does not block on LSP startup. |

items.impact: Unavailable LSP can be represented as omitted, passed, failed, or unmet depending on implementation, changing tier promotion and reporting.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must define a first-class skip state and its aggregation, evidence, UI, and promotion semantics.

items.title: Subagent bias ranking is under-specified for mixed diagnostics
items.statement: The source says to derive languages and prefer matching agents but does not specify weighting, aggregation, deterministic tie-breaking, or behavior when multiple languages, servers, or matching agents are present.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Documentation:** This behavior is specified in **Plans/orchestrator-subagent-integration.md** (Subagent selection from LSP) and summarized here. Implement in the same place that performs `select_for_node`: after building node context, optionally call LSP client `get_diagnostics_for_paths(scope_paths)`; from the returned diagnostics, derive language(s) from `source` or from file extension → server id mapping; then bias subagent selection toward matching language (e.g. add to ProjectContext or NodeContext: "prefer_subagents": ["rust-engineer"] when Rust errors present).
- LSP bias is a **tie-breaker / ranking hint**, not an absolute selector.

items.impact: Equivalent node context can select different subagents across implementations and runs without an explainable invariant.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must define diagnostic aggregation, server-to-language mapping authority, ranking weight, and stable tie-breaks.

items.title: Subagent file-scope default conflicts with preferred order
items.statement: The initial decision defaults subagent bias to changed files, while the canonical rule later prefers an explicit node file list before changed and open files; no rule explains whether the ordered list replaces or merely supplements the default.

evidence.exact_quote: - Default: **changed in last iteration** for consistency with LSP gate.
- Preferred scope order is: explicit node file list -> changed files in current node -> open files.

items.impact: Bias inputs vary depending on which sentence a builder treats as authoritative.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must decide whether explicit node files are the normal first choice, an override, or a fallback and define empty-list behavior.

items.title: Warning-inclusive bias has no configuration contract
items.statement: The canonical rules permit Warning diagnostics when configured, but no config key, enum, default-resolution path, or GUI surface for that option is defined.

evidence.exact_quote: - Default bias threshold is diagnostics with severity `Error`; implementations MAY optionally include `Warning` when configured.

items.impact: Warning-based selection behavior cannot be configured portably or audited from a known setting.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must invent a key and persistence surface or decline the optional behavior.

items.title: Bias explainability is optional
items.statement: Persistence of bias inputs and outcome is only SHOULD-level, so the behavior can affect agent selection without a mandatory audit record.

evidence.exact_quote: - The chosen bias inputs and outcome SHOULD be persisted in run metadata or verification evidence so selection remains explainable.

items.impact: A consequential ranking input can be unavailable during incident review or reproducibility checks.
items.builder_discretion: A builder may omit persistence entirely or choose either metadata or evidence with no required schema.

items.title: Functional acceptance oracles are missing
items.statement: The PlanUnit acceptance and validation surfaces prove source preservation and index validity, but they do not test gate threshold behavior, boundary injection, snapshot completeness, failure paths, UI persistence, or subagent ranking.

evidence.exact_quote: - The covered source span remains losslessly available for exact-text audit.
- python3 scripts/pm-plan-migration.py validate --run-dir Plans/.plan_migration/pds-20260611-002-atomize-planunits
- python3 scripts/pm-plan-index.py validate

items.impact: The plan can pass every named validator while the runtime behavior remains incorrect or unimplemented.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must invent executable tests, fixtures, expected GateReport/evidence records, and UI persistence checks.

items.title: Timeout authority is not wired through the API
items.statement: The config default is ten seconds, while the conceptual diagnostics API has no timeout parameter and separately cites fifteen seconds as an example; injection and precedence are not fixed.

evidence.exact_quote: - `timeout_seconds`: **10** (LSP query timeout)
- Signature (conceptual): `get_diagnostics_for_paths(paths: &[PathBuf], project_root: &Path) -> Result<Vec<LspDiagnosticEntry>, LspGateError>`.

- Returns: list of diagnostics (path, line, character, severity, message, source) for the given paths. If a path has no server or no diagnostics, it contributes an empty list. The client uses the existing DiagnosticsCache (from `publishDiagnostics`) and/or triggers a request if needed; must respect timeout (e.g. 15 s) and return partial results or error on timeout.

items.impact: The verifier and client can enforce different timeouts, producing inconsistent failure timing and partial evidence.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must choose whether timeout is an API argument, injected client state, or outer verifier deadline and reconcile nested deadlines.

items.title: Snapshot filename identity and collision rules are not resolved
items.statement: Two filename forms are offered, but the required timestamp format, sanitization, uniqueness strategy, and authoritative gate/run identifiers are not selected.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Filename:** `lsp-snapshot-{gate_id}-{timestamp}.json` or `lsp-snapshot-{tier_id}-{session_id}.json` so it is unique and tied to the gate run.

items.impact: Concurrent or repeated evaluations can collide or produce artifacts that cannot be deterministically located from a gate report.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must choose the filename form and define collision-safe atomic creation and identifier encoding.

dimension_assessments.summary: Boundary execution, failure routing, capture timing, and fallback behavior are stated, but changed-file intervals and diagnostic freshness leave observable behavior non-deterministic.
The accepted PlanUnit enumerates the core LSP capability inventory and a separate PlanUnit preserves per-feature behavior and fallback coverage.
Paths, project root, diagnostic entries, and snapshot shape are described, but completeness metadata, coordinate encoding, and timeout injection are unresolved.
Gate and evidence contracts are extensive, but blocking and unavailable enum conflicts plus unresolved config precedence prevent a single exact implementation.
Failure transitions to retry, escalation, or stop are explicit, but skip is not defined as a first-class aggregated criterion state.
Verifier, registry, gate-runner, and document ownership are assigned, but configuration authority across redb, VerificationConfig, project JSON, and tier overrides is unresolved.
LSPSupport owns the preserved LSP behavior, VerifierRegistry/LspGateVerifier own evaluation dispatch, and ContractRefs retain cross-document boundaries.
GateReport, EvidenceStore, UI, and subagent selection consume the outputs, but subagent ranking and explainability rules are incomplete.
The Verification controls, notification path, and authored-versus-server copy boundary are explicitly specified.
Timeout, no-server, empty-scope, unavailable-client, retry, escalation, and stop behavior are covered, but evidence-write failure and skip aggregation are missing.
The snapshot contract permits absolute paths and project-root persistence without redaction, permission, retention, or deletion controls.
VerifierResult propagates evidence into GateReport and LSP diagnostics can propagate into subagent ranking, but bias evidence is optional and ranking propagation is under-specified.
Directory, capture timing, timeout, and artifact attachment are stated, but storage failure, filename collision, and deadline wiring lack operational contracts.
Defaults favor changed files, a timeout exists, and prompt ingestion is capped at five items, but project-scope bounds and evidence ranking/summarization are not executable.
Source lineage, exact-token preservation, dual-copy boundaries, and migration validators are explicit, but conflicting serialized enums lack alias or migration rules.
Plan migration and index validators are named, but there are no functional oracles for the LSP gate, evidence, failure, GUI persistence, or subagent-bias behavior.
Builders retain consequential choices over enum normalization, config merge order, scope bounds, freshness, evidence schema and privacy, skip state, ranking, and storage recovery.

The authoritative core contains direct token and enum conflicts plus unresolved temporal scope, evidence completeness, configuration authority, and ranking semantics; no unsupported external assumptions were used to close them.
